### Summary

The kernel's face density is not the face value of its own cell density, so the solver's face density carries
the offset @eq-ch05-refkernel-offset. That offset enters the $x_1$ mass flux at linear order and, through it, the
gravity work. The switch removes it with one operator: it replaces the face density by the face value of the
kernel's own cell density, taken from the quartic through the primitive of that cell field, so that face and cell
are consistent by construction. Nothing else is replaced. The cell density reference, the cell pressure and the
face pressures, and so the rest state, are the kernel's on any grid.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Makes the reference face density the face value of the kernel's own cell density, @eq-ch05-wbref4-face.

**Data.** Reads $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ of the kernel; replaces $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ only.

**Placement.** Inside `HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1`: the resolution flag right after the kernel, the faces after the seam exchange.

**Activation.** Environment variable `SNAP_WB_REF4` (or `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`), default off; needs $n_g\ge3$.

**Guarantee / limits.** $\eta_{\rho,f}=O(\Delta x_1^4)$ where no guard fires; $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$, $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ and so the rest balance are unchanged.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch05-wbref4-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\Pi$ [kg m$^{-2}$] the primitive of the cell reference
density; $i_0$ the first cell of a stencil window, $l$ the cell offset in it and $l_{\mathrm f}$ the face offset; $\ell_{l_{\mathrm f}}$
the Lagrange basis polynomial of face $i_0+l_{\mathrm f}$; $\tilde p$ [Pa] the cubic through four face pressures; $\zeta$ a
Gauss-Legendre node; $n_{\mathrm{poly}}$ the polytropic index and $\mathcal S_i$ [J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$] the entropy
tendency of cell $i$, both in the order test. $\vartheta$[^rg-3739b5b2fec3], $\lambda_w$[^rg-cf66429c8e8b], $\chi$, $\eta_{\rho,f}$, $\mathcal W$, $\Delta x_1$, $n_g$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ are defined in @sec-appa
or @sec-ch05-refkernel.

Guards keep the kernel's face value wherever the new one would leave the range of its two neighbouring cells or
the column is under-resolved, and the face part runs after the seam exchange of @sec-ch05-seam. With the corrected-PE[^rg-36523dc32e4e] face
work of @sec-ch06 on (its default with `gravity-work: face`), the one-step spurious stratification of a neutral column
converges at about fourth order with the switch and second order without it.

*Aliases.* "Leg W" in the centroid derivation note; `SNAPY_WB_REF_EXACT` in the specification.[^ch05-wb4-alias]

[^ch05-wb4-alias]: `docs/derivations/x1-centroid-spherical.md`; `sources/gw__NEXTPR_spec_wbref_exact.md`.

### Derivation

Notation as in @sec-ch05-refkernel; indices are cell indices and $\chi_i=\overline\rho_i/\overline p_i$. The derivation is
that of the derivation note,[^ch05-wb4-note] re-written here and checked by `[C3]`, `[C7]`, `[C8]`, `[C14]`.

[^ch05-wb4-note]: `docs/derivations/wb-ref4.md@919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274` §§2-7.

#### Why only the face value

$\eta_{\rho,f}=\rho_{\mathrm{sf},f}-\mathcal W[\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}]_f$ of @eq-ch05-refkernel-offset is the offset
between the kernel's face density and the face value of the kernel's own cell density. What the solver puts on the face is
$\mathcal W[\overline\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}]_f+\rho_{\mathrm{sf},f}=\mathcal W[\overline\rho]_f+\eta_{\rho,f}$, by
linearity of the reconstruction. So the face density is a consistent high-order face value exactly when
$\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ is the face value of the cell field $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$, **whatever the accuracy of
$\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ itself**: a bias shared by the cell reference and its face value is subtracted and added back
and cannot reach the flux. One operator therefore closes the offset, and the switch replaces nothing else. The
cell density reference stays the kernel's $p_{\mathrm{ref}}\chi^{s}$ of @eq-ch05-refkernel-dens, and so does
every pressure.

#### Face density

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\mathrm{sf},f} &= \partial_1 \Pi(x_{1,f}), \\
\Pi(x_{1,i_0+l_{\mathrm f}}) &= \sum_{l<l_{\mathrm f}}\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0+l}\,\Delta x_{1,i_0+l},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbref4-face}

with $\Pi$ the quartic through the primitive at the five faces $l_{\mathrm f}=0..4$ (four cells), window $i_0=f-2$ kept inside the owned cells at a
clamped wall, physical spacing. On a uniform grid of width $\Delta x_1$, $\Pi$ takes the values $0,\ \Delta x_1\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0},\ \Delta x_1(\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0}+\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0+1}),\dots$
at the faces $l_{\mathrm f}=0..4$; writing $\Pi$ in the Lagrange basis $\ell_{l_{\mathrm f}}$ of those five faces and differentiating,
$\rho_{\mathrm{sf},i_0+l_{\mathrm f}}=\partial_1\Pi(x_{1,i_0+l_{\mathrm f}})=\sum_{l=0}^{3}\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0+l}\,\Delta x_1\sum_{l'_{\mathrm f}>l}\partial_1\ell_{l'_{\mathrm f}}(x_{1,i_0+l_{\mathrm f}})$, which on
$\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0..i_0+3}$ is $(25,-23,13,-3)/12$ at $l_{\mathrm f}=0$ (the wall face), $(3,13,-5,1)/12$ at $l_{\mathrm f}=1$ (the next) and
$(-1,7,7,-1)/12$ at $l_{\mathrm f}=2$ (the interior face, window $i_0=f-2$) (`[C8]`). The face is exact for cubic
point profiles on any grid, so $\eta_{\rho,f}=\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}-\mathcal W[\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}]=O(\Delta x_1^4)$ (`[C14]`:
mid-column offset $3.22\times10^{-12}$, $5.18\times10^{-14}$, $6.91\times10^{-16}$ relative at $n_1$ = 32, 64, 128, orders
5.96 and 6.23, against order 2.00 for the kernel; at $n_1=256$ it is at round-off level, $1.38\times10^{-16}$ in this run, so
that level measures round-off, not truncation). @eq-ch05-wbref4-face is built as the weights `awt`
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_stencils >}})
and applied by `wb_ref4_faces`
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_faces >}}).

#### Cell pressure and cell density

The switch changes no cell value, on any grid: `wb_ref4_faces` writes only $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_faces >}}), and `wb_ref4_flag` reads the scan pressures and returns a
boolean ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_flag >}}). On a uniform grid the cell pressure is the six-face
pressure of @eq-ch05-refkernel-pref; on a keyed stretched $x_1$ it is the six-face average built from the widths,
@eq-ch05-refkernel-stretched, of sixth order. The rest state is therefore the kernel's with the switch on or off,
and `balance_column` does not call the switch (@sec-ch05-balcol). The stencils of the face part use the face
positions (physical spacing), so they apply to a stretched $x_1$ as built.

#### Guards and rest balance

A face whose new value lies outside the range of its two neighbouring cell references keeps the kernel's face,
with relative margin $10^{-10}$. A cell with $\lvert\ln(p_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2}/p_{\mathrm{sf},i+1/2})\rvert>0.5$,
fewer than two cells per pressure scale height, is flagged, the flag is dilated by two cells, and a face with a
flagged cell on either side keeps the kernel's value; ghosts past a clamped wall do not count. The flag reads
$p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ at most three cells away, which is why $n_g\ge3$ is required: then both sides of an $x_1$ seam
compute the same flag. The threshold, dilation and margin are design choices, not derived. Since neither
$p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ nor $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ nor $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is changed, the rest state
@eq-ch05-wbx1-rest is the kernel's.

*Why the two sides of an $x_1$ seam agree.* Three steps.

1. *The flag is local.* `wb_ref4_flag` reads only the block's own scan pressures, so it needs no exchange; it is
   built right after the kernel ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_flag >}}).
2. *The face part reads only exchanged cells.* `wb_ref4_faces` runs after the seam exchange of
   $(p_{\mathrm{ref}},\rho_{\mathrm{ref}})$, and its four-cell window at an interior face reaches two cells past the
   face, inside $n_g\ge2$. The flag of a cell is dilated by two cells (`max_pool1d` of width 5), so a face next to a
   seam depends on scan pressures up to three cells away; with $n_g\ge3$ both blocks hold them, which is the setup
   check.
3. *The guard does not flip on round-off.* `in_range` widens each bound by `kMargin` $=10^{-10}$ relative, far above
   the round-off of the next paragraph, so a split column and one block take the same branch on a flat profile,
   where the two bounds coincide.

*Round-off.* The face weights are computed in double by `lagrange_deriv`, so they carry a rounding of their own
that is not bounded here; their four-term sum adds at most $4\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_l\lvert a_l\rvert\max\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}
=\tfrac{16}{3}\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\max\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ in the interior, with $\sum_l\lvert a_l\rvert=16/12$ for the
weights $a_l=(-1,7,7,-1)/12$. The $n_1=256$ level of `[C14]`, at round-off level, lies inside it.

*Exact and truncated.* Exact: the face weights for cubics. $O(\Delta x_1^4)$: $\eta_{\rho,f}$ in the interior. At the
three faces next to a wall the note gives $O(\Delta x_1^3)$ (the anchor constant through the even ghosts); not
re-checked here. The cell reference keeps the kernel's second-order bias, which @eq-ch05-refkernel-dens carries and
which cancels out of the face value by the argument above.

### Numerical method

The stencil is shown in @fig-ch05-wbref4-stencils. The stencils and weights are built once per block, on the CPU in double
precision, and cached until device or dtype changes; application is a gather and a weighted sum on the block's device.
The resolution flag is built right after the kernel in `_hydro_ref_x1`; the face part runs after the seam ghost-row
exchange, so a column split along $x_1$ gets the same faces as one block. A block with a clamped wall and fewer than
four owned cells keeps the kernel's reference.

### Code

**A minimal input.** The switch is an environment variable, not a YAML key. A deck it acts on needs gravity along
$x_1$, three ghost cells and, for the wall stencils, the wall clamp:

```yaml
geometry:
  type: cartesian
  bounds: {x1min: 0., x1max: 1.e4}
  cells: {nx1: 64, nghost: 3}   # three ghost cells: the setup check below
dynamics:
  wb-wall-clamp: true           # the default; the wall stencils use owned cells only
forcing:
  const-gravity: {grav1: -9.8}
```

With these keys in a copy of `straka_single.yaml`, saved as `deck.yaml` in `build/bin` of a build at the pin
([Install and run](#sec-preface-install)), run

```bash
SNAP_WB_REF4=1 ./straka.release deck.yaml
```

A PyPI release of snapy has no such switch and ignores the variable without a message.

**What it refuses, and why.** Setup refuses $n_g<3$ with gravity on
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}), because the flag of step 3 above would then read
cells a block does not hold, and the two sides of a seam could disagree. Values of `SNAP_WB_REF4` other than empty,

fewer than five cells in all, is not refused: its stencils are marked unusable

### Summary

A finite-volume cell on a spherical-polar grid holds the $r^2$ mean of a quantity, whose centroid sits
$\Delta x_1^2/(6r^{\mathrm m}_i)$ above the mid-radius $r^{\mathrm m}_i$. Every $x_1$ cell-to-face map of the solver, from the WENO weights to the
scan and the six-face cell pressure, is a formula for plain means. Fed $r^2$ means they are off by $O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$: the face
values, the scan step, and the pressure force, whose plain difference balances gravity only against the wrong scan.
The switch converts the inputs of the maps, for the maps only, to plain means with a five-cell stencil exact to degree
4, and makes the radial pressure force the $r^2$ mean of the gradient of a quintic through six face pressures. The
reference on plain means is then the Cartesian one, and the switch implies `SNAP_WB_REF4` so that it is fourth order.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Feeds every $x_1$ map plain means instead of $r^2$ means, and makes the pressure source exact, @eq-ch05-x1cent-source.

**Data.** Reads the $r^2$ means and the face pressures; gives plain means to the $x_1$ maps and $S_i$ to the momentum source.

**Placement.** The $x_1$ sweep of `HydroImpl::forward` and `SphericalPolarImpl::forward`, every RK stage.

**Activation.** Environment variable `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`, default off; acts on `spherical-polar`; implies `SNAP_WB_REF4`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Rest exact for densities of degree $\le4$; ratios of means keep $O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$ (@sec-ch05-oneoverr).

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch05-x1cent-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\langle q\rangle_i$ the $r^2$ mean and $\overline q_i$ the plain mean of cell $i$; $r^{\mathrm m}_i$ [m] the
mid-radius and $\Delta$ [m] the width $\Delta x_{1,i}$; $x$ [-] the local coordinate; $c_{i,l}$ [-] the conversion
weights and $c^S_{i,l}$ [m$^{-1}$] the source weights over the window starting at cell or face $i_0$, offset $l$;
$d_{\mathrm{mon}}$ the monomial degree; $\tilde p$ [Pa] the quintic through six face pressures; $S_i$ [Pa m$^{-1}$] the radial
pressure source. $\delta_i$[^rg-929a9e6df954], $A_{i\pm1/2}$[^rg-4cb11b837953], $V_i$[^rg-928038c8e04b], $p^{*}$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ are defined in @sec-appa.

On Cartesian blocks the switch only implies `SNAP_WB_REF4`; on cubed-sphere blocks it does nothing (their $x_{1v}$ is
the mid-radius). `balance_column` balances only a column declared Cartesian under it.

*Aliases.* "the centroid switch"; legs (i)-(iii) in the comments of `x1_centroid.hpp`.

### Derivation

Units: $r$[^rg-2ecd0b8c12cb] and $\Delta x_1$ [m]; $A_{i\pm1/2}=r_{i\pm1/2}^2$ and $V_i=(r_{i+1/2}^3-r_{i-1/2}^3)/3$ are per unit solid angle, as the
code forms them. $\langle q\rangle_i=V_i^{-1}\int r^2q\,\mathrm{d}r$ is the $r^2$ mean, $\overline q_i=\Delta x_{1,i}^{-1}\int q\,\mathrm{d}r$ the plain
mean, and $x=(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)/\Delta x_{1,i}$ the local coordinate, with $r^{\mathrm m}_i=\tfrac12(r_{i-1/2}+r_{i+1/2})$ the mid-radius (appendix A $x^{\mathrm m}_{1,i}$[^rg-9f1279c76a64]). Re-written from the derivation note.[^ch05-x1c-note]

[^ch05-x1c-note]: `docs/derivations/x1-centroid-spherical.md@919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274` §§1-5.

#### The defect

Write $r^{\mathrm m}_i=\tfrac12(r_{i-1/2}+r_{i+1/2})$ for the mid-radius and $\Delta=\Delta x_{1,i}$. Expanding $q$ about
$r^{\mathrm m}_i$, $q(r)=q+(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)\,\partial_1q+\tfrac12(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2\,\partial_1^2q+\tfrac16(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)^3\,\partial_1^3q+\dots$,
with $q$ and its derivatives taken at $r^{\mathrm m}_i$, the two means need the moments of $r-r^{\mathrm m}_i$ on each
measure. With $\int r^2\,\mathrm dr=\Delta\big((r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2+\Delta^2/12\big)$ and
$\int(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)\,r^2\,\mathrm dr=r^{\mathrm m}_i\Delta^3/6$ over the cell,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta_i &= \langle r-r^{\mathrm m}_i\rangle_i = \frac{r^{\mathrm m}_i\Delta^3/6}{\Delta\big((r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2+\Delta^2/12\big)}
 = \frac{2\Delta^2\,r^{\mathrm m}_i}{\Delta^2+12\,(r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2}
 = \frac{\Delta^2}{6r^{\mathrm m}_i}-\frac{\Delta^4}{72\,(r^{\mathrm m}_i)^3}+\cdots, \\
\langle (r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2\rangle_i &= \frac{\Delta^2}{12}+\frac{\Delta^4}{180\,(r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2}+\cdots,
\qquad \overline{(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2}_i=\frac{\Delta^2}{12},\qquad \overline{(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)}_i=0,
\end{aligned}
$$

so that

$$
\langle q\rangle_i = \overline q_i + \delta_i\,\partial_1 q(r^{\mathrm m}_i)
+ \frac{\Delta^4}{240\,r^{\mathrm m}_i}\,\partial_1^3q + \frac{\Delta^4}{360\,(r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2}\,\partial_1^2q + O(\Delta^6),
$$ {#eq-ch05-x1cent-defect}

$\delta_i$ being the centroid offset of appendix A (`[C18]`, exact). The second-moment difference gives the last term
and the third moment $\langle(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)^3\rangle_i=\Delta^4/(40\,r^{\mathrm m}_i)+\dots$ the one before it, so the
remainder after $\delta_i\partial_1q$ is $O(\Delta x_1^4/r)$. Each uniform-measure map fed $\langle q\rangle$ is off by
$\delta_i\partial_1q=O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$; in particular the scan step becomes $g\Delta x_1\langle\rho\rangle$ instead of
$g\int\rho\,\mathrm{d}r=g\Delta x_1\overline\rho$, and the perturbation of a resting column is $O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$ instead of
a constant.

#### Plain means

For the $x_1$ maps only, each primitive row is replaced by

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overline q_i &= \sum_{l=0}^{4} c_{i,l}\,\langle q\rangle_{i_0+l}, \\
\sum_l c_{i,l}\,\langle x^{d_{\mathrm{mon}}}\rangle_{i_0+l} &= \overline{x^{d_{\mathrm{mon}}}}_i = \big(1,\ 0,\ \tfrac1{12},\ 0,\ \tfrac1{80}\big)_{d_{\mathrm{mon}}},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-x1cent-conv}

for the monomial degrees $d_{\mathrm{mon}}=0..4$, window $i_0=\max(\mathrm{lo},\min(\mathrm{hi}-4,i-2))$, centred, inside the owned cells at a physical wall and inside the
array at a seam. The moments are integrated by four-point Gauss-Legendre, exact to degree 7 while every integrand has degree at most 6, and the $5\times5$ system
is solved once per block. The conversion is exact for degree 4 and not 5, on uniform and stretched grids and in the
wall windows, and its weights sum to 1 (`[C16]`). @eq-ch05-x1cent-conv is `x1_plain_mean_stencils`
({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_plain_mean_stencils >}}).
Ghosts past a physical wall get the mirrored correction of the owned cells, odd for the normal velocity unless the
boundary is `outflow`, in
`x1_plain_means`
({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_plain_means >}});
at a seam the outer ghosts' windows are off-centre, so their plain means are replaced by the neighbour's.

#### The pressure source

With $\tilde p$ the quintic through the six face pressures nearest cell $i$ (window over faces, one-sided at a wall,
reaching two faces past a seam), the radial pressure source is

$$
S_i = \frac{2}{V_i}\int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}} r\,\tilde p\,\mathrm{d}r = \sum_{l=0}^{5}c^S_{i,l}\,p^{*}_{i_0+l},
$$ {#eq-ch05-x1cent-source}

and integration by parts gives the net pressure force. Since $\partial_r(r^2\tilde p)=2r\tilde p+r^2\partial_r\tilde p$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
S_iV_i = 2\int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}} r\,\tilde p\,\mathrm{d}r
&= \big[r^2\tilde p\big]_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}} - \int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}} r^2\,\partial_r\tilde p\,\mathrm{d}r \\
&= A_{i+1/2}p^{*}_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2}p^{*}_{i-1/2} - \int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}} r^2\,\partial_r\tilde p\,\mathrm{d}r ,
\end{aligned}
$$

where the second line uses that $\tilde p$ passes through both faces of the cell, $\tilde p(r_{i\pm1/2})=p^{*}_{i\pm1/2}$,
and $A_{i\pm1/2}=r_{i\pm1/2}^2$. Dividing by $V_i$,
$-(A_{i+1/2}p^{*}_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2}p^{*}_{i-1/2})/V_i+S_i=-V_i^{-1}\int r^2\,\partial_r\tilde p\,\mathrm{d}r$: the net pressure force is
the $r^2$ mean of $-\partial_r\tilde p$. A constant pressure gives $S_iV_i=A_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2}$ exactly, with $V_i$ in the
cube form of the cell volume (`[C17]`, both identities in exact rationals). @eq-ch05-x1cent-source is
`x1_pressure_source_stencils`
({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_pressure_source_stencils >}}),
used in place of the plain difference by the branch that tests `exact_x1`
({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}}).
The hydrostatic mode takes the same operator (@sec-ch05-hsmode).

#### Rest balance

On a hydrostatic column of $r^2$ means: the conversion gives $\overline\rho$ to $O(\Delta x_1^6/r)$; the scan then gives the
exact face pressures plus one constant; the reference on plain means is the Cartesian fourth-order one; and the net
force $-V^{-1}\int r^2(\partial_r\tilde p+g\rho)\,\mathrm{d}r$ has the constant drop out. For a density of degree $\le4$ every step
is exact and the column is balanced exactly, which is the oracle of the test.

*Exact and truncated.* Exact: the conversion for degree 4, both source identities, rest for degree $\le4$. For a
smooth column the curvature part of the residual is $O(\Delta x_1^6/r)$; what remains is the truncation of the reference itself.
Ratios of means (the Favre velocity, $T=p/\rho$, $\chi$ inside $\mathsf F$) are not made exact (@sec-ch05-oneoverr); for the
velocity, `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE` subtracts the covariance part (@sec-ch04-x1masscov).

*Why a resting column of $r^2$ means stays at rest.* Four steps, each a line of the code.

1. *The maps read plain means.* `HydroImpl::forward` hands `wx1 = x1_plain_means(...)` to `_hydro_ref_x1` and to the
   reconstruction, and the conserved state keeps its $r^2$ means: `wx1` is a separate tensor. Plain means are
   averages in $r$, so under the switch `HydroImpl::reset` gives the $x_1$ reconstruction of a spherical-polar block
   the per-face rows of the $r$ faces `x1f` on a keyed stretched $x_1$, and leaves it on its uniform weights
   otherwise; it does not use the volume-coordinate rows that `x1_row_faces` returns without the switch
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).
2. *The seam ghosts are the neighbour's.* `_x1_ghost_rows(wx1, ...)` replaces the off-centre ghost windows, so a split
   column converts like one block.
3. *The source is the exact $r$-moment.* With the face pressures defined, `SphericalPolarImpl::forward` adds
   `x1_pressure_source` instead of the plain-difference correction, and its weights divide by the cube-form volume
   `(xf[i+1]^3 - xf[i]^3)/3` that `cell_volume()` uses, so a constant pressure exerts no force.
4. *The reference is then Cartesian.* On plain means the scan and @sec-ch05-wbref4 are the Cartesian operators, and
   the net force is the $r^2$ mean of $-(\partial_r\tilde p+g\rho)$, zero for degree $\le4$.

*Round-off.* The conversion is a five-term sum, so by the dot-product bound $\overline q_i$ carries at most
$5\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_l\lvert c_{i,l}\rvert\max\lvert\langle q\rangle\rvert$ besides the rounding of the weights from
the $5\times5$ solve, which is not bounded here; for $\Delta\ll r$ the weights approach the plain fourth-order
ones and $\sum_l\lvert c_{i,l}\rvert$ stays of order 1. The pressure force is the source minus the flux divergence, two terms each of size about
$p/\Delta x_1$ (since $A/V\approx1/\Delta x_1$). For the constant-pressure identity of @eq-ch05-x1cent-source the
rounding count is, to first order with $\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ per operation:

1. *The flux difference.* $(r_{i+1/2}^2p-r_{i-1/2}^2p)/V_i$ rounds the two squares and the two products, each by
   $\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ of a term of size $r^2p/V_i\approx p/\Delta x_1$: at most $2\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\,p/\Delta x_1$. The
   subtraction and the division round the difference, of size $2p/r$, and add $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}p/r$.
2. *The source.* `apply` sums six products, so by the dot-product bound it carries at most
   $3\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_l\lvert c^S_{i,l}\rvert p$, of size $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}p/r$ since $c^S\sim 1/r$.
3. *The common volume.* $V_i$ divides both terms, so its rounding scales the net force, not the two large terms.
4. *Hence* $\lvert S_i-(A_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2})p/V_i\rvert\le2\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\,p/\Delta x_1$ for $r\gg\Delta x_1$. A float64 port of
   `x1_pressure_source_stencils` measures at most $0.90\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\,p/\Delta x_1$ at $r_0$ = 5, 60 and 1000
   (`derivation_check.py`, `XC-4`), inside it. In units of $g\rho$ the bound is $2\epsilon_{\mathrm m}H_p/\Delta x_1$, with
   $H_p=p/(\rho g)$ the pressure scale height.

The rest test's column ($\rho=1-0.3(r-r_0)$, $g=1$, $\Delta x_1=1/16$) has $H_p/\Delta x_1$ between 38 and 40, so the
bound is $1.8\times10^{-14}$ in units of $g\rho$; its rest forces with the switch, $0.86$ to $3.3\times10^{-14}$
(@tbl-ch05-x1cent-rest), include the rounding of the reconstruction, the Riemann flux and the gravity source as well.

**Not provided:** a round-off bound for that complete rest-force calculation; the operation count above
is limited to the constant-pressure flux/source identity and excludes those additional operations.

### Numerical method

The windows are shown in @fig-ch05-x1cent-window. In `HydroImpl::forward` the plain-mean view `wx1` is computed before the
reference, its seam ghost rows are taken from the neighbour, and the reconstruction and the reference read it; the
primitives themselves are unchanged. After the Riemann solve the two ghost face pressures each side of a seam are taken
from the neighbour, so the source window is the centred one-block window. Everything runs in every RK stage,
explicitly; the stencils are built once per block in double precision.

### Summary

On a spherical-polar grid the $r^2$ cell measure adds terms of relative size $\Delta x_1/r$ to every cell-to-face map, and the
divergence adds a $2/r$ factor to every flux error. The covariance corrections of @sec-ch04 and the plain-mean maps
of @sec-ch05-x1cent remove the leading such terms of the face fluxes, the reference and the pressure force. What remains
is not a defect of any map but of an input: the $x_1$ velocity the maps reconstruct is a ratio of two $r^2$ means, not a
mean, and the conversion of @eq-ch05-x1cent-conv makes means plain, not ratios exact. This section records that
remainder, its signature, and what evidence exists for it; it has no code of its own.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** States the $O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$ error left once the plain-mean maps are on: a Favre velocity treated as a mean.

**Data.** None of its own; measured as the $1/r$ content of the one-step effective stratification.

**Placement.** The $x_1$ reconstruction in `HydroImpl::forward`, through the velocity it is fed.

**Activation.** Always present on spherical-polar grids; `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE` subtracts its velocity part.

**Guarantee / limits.** $O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$; the $T=p/\rho$ and $\chi$ ratios keep it, with no switch.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch05-oneoverr-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\tilde v_{1,i}$ [m s$^{-1}$] the stored Favre velocity $\langle\rho v_1\rangle_i/\langle\rho\rangle_i$;
$r_0$ [m] the radius of the column's base; $L_z$ [m] the column depth (not appendix A's scale height $H$); $D$ [-] the $1/r$ content defined in the Numerical
method; $\eta_{\mathrm{ro}}$ [-] the round-off of one value of $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eff}}n_1^2$. $\langle\cdot\rangle$,
$\overline{\,\cdot\,}$, $r^{\mathrm m}_i$ and $\delta_i$ are those of @sec-ch05-x1cent; $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is
appendix A's one-step effective onset error.

*Aliases.* "the 1/R term"; "leg (d)" and "hypothesis H1" in the sources.[^ch05-1r-alias]

[^ch05-1r-alias]: Leg (d) in the comments of `x1_centroid.hpp`; hypothesis H1 of `sources/gw__ONEOVERR_split_RESULT.md`.

### Derivation

Notation as in @sec-ch05-x1cent. The stored velocity of cell $i$ is the
Favre mean $\tilde v_{1,i}=\langle\rho v_1\rangle_i/\langle\rho\rangle_i$. Expand $\rho$ and $v_1$ about the mid-radius $r^{\mathrm m}_i$, with derivatives there and the moments of
@eq-ch05-x1cent-defect, $\langle r-r^{\mathrm m}_i\rangle_i=\delta_i$ and $\langle(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2\rangle_i=\Delta x_{1,i}^2/12+O(\Delta x_1^4/r^2)$.
Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\langle\rho\rangle_i &= \rho+\delta_i\,\partial_1\rho+\tfrac{\Delta x_{1,i}^2}{24}\,\partial_1^2\rho+\dots, \\
\langle\rho v_1\rangle_i &= \rho v_1+\delta_i\,\partial_1(\rho v_1)+\tfrac{\Delta x_{1,i}^2}{24}\,\partial_1^2(\rho v_1)+\dots, \\
\tilde v_{1,i}=\frac{\langle\rho v_1\rangle_i}{\langle\rho\rangle_i}
&= v_1+\delta_i\,\partial_1v_1+\frac{\Delta x_{1,i}^2}{12}\,\frac{\partial_1\rho\,\partial_1v_1}{\rho}+\frac{\Delta x_{1,i}^2}{24}\,\partial_1^2v_1+\dots,
\end{aligned}
$$

using $\partial_1^2(\rho v_1)=v_1\partial_1^2\rho+2\partial_1\rho\,\partial_1v_1+\rho\,\partial_1^2v_1$ in the quotient, while the plain mean is
$\overline v_{1,i}=v_1+\tfrac{\Delta x_{1,i}^2}{24}\,\partial_1^2v_1+O(\Delta x_1^4)$. Subtracting, the $\partial_1^2v_1$ terms cancel:

$$
\tilde v_{1,i} - \overline v_{1,i} = \frac{\Delta x_{1,i}^2}{12}\,\frac{\partial_1\rho\,\partial_1 v_1}{\rho} + \delta_i\,\partial_1 v_1 + O(\Delta x_1^4) ,
$$ {#eq-ch05-oneoverr-favre}

where the first term is the Cartesian covariance of a density-weighted mean, whose identity is derived in
@sec-ch04-x1masscov, and the second the centroid offset of the $r^2$ measure ($\partial_1$ is the radial derivative
here, $x_1=r$; derived for linear $\rho$ and $v_1$ in `[C21]`, exact in sympy). The conversion of @eq-ch05-x1cent-conv
treats $\tilde v_1$ as an $r^2$ mean and so removes the $\delta_i\partial_1 v_1$ part; the covariance part stays
unless `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE` is set, which subtracts $\tfrac{1}{12}\Delta x_{1,i}^2\,\partial_1\rho\,\partial_1 v_1/\rho$
from the reconstructed velocity ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::x1_mass_covariance >}},
@sec-ch04-x1masscov).
Reconstructing the converted value with weights for plain means therefore leaves an $O(\Delta x_1^2)$ face error,
which the $2/r$ of the radial divergence turns into an $O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$ tendency. The
same holds for $T=p/\rho$ and for $\chi$ inside the reference filter. The remainder shows in the effective
stratification with the signature $+g/(6c_pr_0)$, and the face fluxes are complete to $O(\Delta x_1^4)$ including
$\Delta x_1^2/r$.[^ch05-1r-src]

[^ch05-1r-src]: The expansion follows `docs/derivations/x1-centroid-spherical.md@919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274` §6; the harness and the
    signature are in `sources/study__next-1overR_README.md` §§0-3; the completeness of the face fluxes is
    `sources/gw__ONEOVERR_split_RESULT.md` §§1-2.

*Why it survives the corrections.* Four steps.

1. *The velocity row is a ratio.* The primitive $x_1$ velocity is the conserved $\langle\rho v_1\rangle$ divided by
   $\langle\rho\rangle$, so the row `w[IVX]` the maps read is $\tilde v_1$, not a mean of $v_1$.
2. *The conversion removes only the measure part.* `x1_plain_means` treats every row as an $r^2$ mean, so it removes
   $\delta_i\partial_1v_1$ and leaves the covariance term of @eq-ch05-oneoverr-favre.
3. *The reconstruction takes it for a plain mean.* WENO5 maps cell values to face values as if they were plain means,
   so the covariance term reaches the face velocity, and with it the mass flux, at $O(\Delta x_1^2)$.
4. *The divergence divides by $r$.* The radial flux difference carries the face areas $r^2_{i\pm1/2}$ over $V_i$,
   which turns that face error into an $O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$ tendency. `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE` removes the velocity's
   share of step 3 only.

*Exact and truncated.* The remainder is $O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$ and vanishes for $r\to\infty$ (Cartesian).

### Summary

Two routines treat a stratified column at a wall without the well-balanced reconstruction: one fills the ghost cells
with an isentropic continuation of the wall cell, the other makes the two states at the wall face agree. The ghost fill's call in `HydroImpl::forward` is commented out; the face copy runs only on the $x_1$ path
taken when `wb_x1` is false and gravity is on, a combination no configuration reaches with a pressure row.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Two wall treatments of the non-well-balanced $x_1$ path: isentropic wall ghosts and a wall-face state copy.

**Data.** The wall ghosts of $p$ and $\rho$, or the left and right states at the wall face (@eq-ch05-legacy-copy).

**Placement.** `HydroImpl::forward`: the ghost fill's call is commented out; the copy follows the $x_1$ reconstruction.

**Activation.** None in practice: with gravity and a pressure row the path of @sec-ch05-wbx1 runs instead.

**Guarantee / limits.** None: kept, not maintained, and not tested.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch05-legacy-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\Upsilon=p^{\alpha_\gamma}$ one cell further down (code `h`); $K_{\mathrm{is}}$ [Pa m$^{3\gamma}$ kg$^{-\gamma}$] the isentrope constant $p/\rho^\gamma$ of the wall cell;
$\alpha_\gamma=(\gamma-1)/\gamma$ [-]; $g=-g_1>0$; $p^{L}$, $p^{R}$, $\rho^{L}$, $\rho^{R}$ the left and right states at
a face. $\gamma$[^rg-04c21cf31c4e] and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ are defined in @sec-appa.

*Why neither routine runs.* Four steps, each a line of `HydroImpl::forward`.

1. *The ghost fill is never called.* Its two calls sit inside a `/* ... */` comment.
2. *The copy is on the other branch.* It runs in the `else` of `if (wb_x1)`, and only when `grav1` is true.
3. *That branch needs gravity without a pressure row.* `wb_x1 = grav1 && w.size(0) > IPR && eos type != "shallow-water"`,
   so with gravity on the `else` is taken only for a state without a pressure row or with `shallow-water`.
4. *Neither has a pressure row for the copy.* `shallow-water` has `nvar() = 4` and `IPR = 4`, so the copy's `wl[IPR]`
   has nothing to act on.

### Derivation

The face copy sets, at the lower wall face $i_s-\tfrac12$ (and symmetrically at the upper one),

$$
\begin{aligned}
p^{L}_{i_s-1/2} &\leftarrow p^{R}_{i_s-1/2}, \\
\rho^{L}_{i_s-1/2} &\leftarrow \rho^{R}_{i_s-1/2},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-legacy-copy}

in `_revise_x1inner_lr`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_revise_x1inner_lr >}}),
so the Riemann solver sees no pressure jump at the wall. The ghost fill holds the wall cell's ratio of specific heats $\gamma$ (`W->A` of that cell) and its
isentrope constant $K_{\mathrm{is}}$ fixed, and integrates hydrostatic balance
$\partial_1p=-\rho g$ with $\rho=(p/K_{\mathrm{is}})^{1/\gamma}$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm d(p^{\alpha_\gamma})}{\mathrm dx_1}=\alpha_\gamma\,p^{\alpha_\gamma-1}\,\partial_1p
=-\alpha_\gamma\,g\,K_{\mathrm{is}}^{-1/\gamma}\,p^{\,\alpha_\gamma-1+1/\gamma}
=-\frac{\alpha_\gamma\,g}{K_{\mathrm{is}}^{1/\gamma}},
$$

since $\alpha_\gamma-1+1/\gamma=0$. So $p^{\alpha_\gamma}$ is linear in $x_1$, and stepping it down by the centre spacing
cell by cell into the ghosts is exact for the isentropic hydrostatic profile, in `_revise_x1inner_ghost`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_revise_x1inner_ghost >}}). `[LG-1]` checks the exponent identity.

*Round-off.* The copy is a copy, exact. Each ghost step forms $\Upsilon=p^{\alpha_\gamma}+\alpha_\gamma g\Delta x_1/K_{\mathrm{is}}^{1/\gamma}$,
a sum of two positive terms, counting $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ per rounding to first order (a correctly rounded `pow` is
assumed, not checked; the constants $\alpha_\gamma$ and $K_{\mathrm{is}}$ are computed once and not counted). The
second term rounds four times: two products, $K_{\mathrm{is}}^{1/\gamma}$ and the division. The first term carries
$\alpha_\gamma$ times the previous step's error $E_{n-1}$ plus its `pow`. The sum adds one, so $\Upsilon$ is off by
at most $\max(\alpha_\gamma E_{n-1}+1,\,4)+1$, and $p=\Upsilon^{1/\alpha_\gamma}$ multiplies that by $1/\alpha_\gamma$ and
adds one: $E_n = \bigl(\max(\alpha_\gamma E_{n-1}+1,\,4)+1\bigr)/\alpha_\gamma+1$, $E_0=0$. For $\gamma=1.4$
($\alpha_\gamma=2/7$) that is $18.5$, $26.5$ and $34.5$ after one, two and three steps, so
$\lvert\Delta p/p\rvert\le34.5\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m}=7.7\times10^{-15}$ for $n_g=3$ (`[LG-2]`).

**The lines that implement @eq-ch05-legacy-copy and the ghost step.** From `_revise_x1inner_lr` and

